content:
Former James Bond star Pierce Brosnan has thrown his support behind Callum Turner as the next 007, singling out the British actor in a new Vanity Fair interview as the race to replace Daniel Craig reaches its final stages.

"Callum Turner is someone I've worked with, and he's so strong," Brosnan said, according to multiple reports of the interview published November 3 and 4. Brosnan, who played Bond in four films from 1995 to 2002, was careful to frame himself as an outsider to the decision, saying: "I'm just an audience member now."

Brosnan and Turner previously shared the screen in the 2017 film The Only Living Boy in New York. Turner is reported to be among a small group of actors who took part in final screen tests in London, alongside Slow Horses star Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor, with reports describing Turner as the bookmakers' favorite. The Hollywood Reporter has suggested between three and five actors were involved in the screen tests, according to Men's Journal.

No official casting announcement has been made. Brosnan himself stressed that he does not know who will get the role, adding: "Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage." Producer Amy Pascal has previously said that the end of the year is "a good bet" for when the world will find out, according to Far Out Magazine.

The next Bond film, known for now as Bond 26, will be directed by Denis Villeneuve from a script by Steven Knight, with a reported target of 2028. Brosnan also praised Villeneuve, saying: "I think we are going to be blown away."

Analysis: An endorsement that matters because of who gives it

Brosnan's words carry weight precisely because he is not campaigning for the job or claiming inside knowledge. A former Bond praising a successor candidate is a familiar ritual, but this one lands differently: Turner is not a stranger to Brosnan, he is a former co-star, and the endorsement arrives just as reports say the final tests are done and a decision is expected by year's end. If Turner gets the role, Brosnan's backing will read as an early blessing from the franchise's past. If he does not, it will still stand as a reminder of how narrow — and how watched — this final shortlist has become. Either way, the waiting game is nearly over.
